source: Pathogen Atlas V2 Phase 4 accepted evidence and Phase 5 IMSTE coordinates

features.label: ANIMAL CONTACT
features.definition: can the infection be transmitted via contact with animals (wild, domesticated or pets)?

features.label: AQUATIC VERTEBRATES
features.definition: is the pathogen associated with fish or amphibians?

features.label: BIRDS
features.definition: is the pathogen associated with birds, either wild or domesticated (chickens, ducks, poultry)?

features.label: DOMESTICATED ANIMALS
features.definition: is the pathogen associated with livestock such as cattle, pigs, chickens or sheep?

features.label: INVERTEBRATES
features.definition: is the pathogen associated with invertebrates such as shellfish, insects or arthropods?

features.label: MAMMALS
features.definition: is the pathogen associated with any (wild) mammal such as rats, rodents, deer, monkeys or bats?

features.label: PETS
features.definition: is the pathogen associated with companion animals such as cats, dogs or hamsters?

features.label: REPTILES
features.definition: is the pathogen associated with reptiles such as snakes or turtles?

features.label: ANAEROBIC
features.definition: is the pathgen a (facultative) anaerobe?

features.label: ASYMPTOMATIC CARRIAGE
features.definition: was the pathogen present but not causing infection prior?

features.label: BIOFILM
features.definition: does the pathogen form a biofilm (on mucal surfaces or implants)?

features.label: MULTIDRUG RESISTANCE
features.definition: is the pathogen resistant to multiple antibiotics?

features.label: SPOREFORMING
features.definition: is the pahogen capable of producing spores or dormant cells?

features.label: TOXINS
features.definition: are symptoms caused by (endo)toxins?

features.label: BACTERAEMIA
features.definition: was the pathogen detected in blood cultures?

features.label: CARDIOVASCULAR
features.definition: does the infection affect the bloodvessel system (such as heartvalves)?

features.label: CUTANEOUS
features.definition: does the infection affect the skin  (such as cellulitis)?

features.label: DIGESTIVE
features.definition: does the infection affect the gastro-intestimal system (such as the gut)?

features.label: ENDOCRINE
features.definition: does the infection affect glands (such as the thyroid glands)?

features.label: LYMPHATIC
features.definition: does the infection affect the lymphatic system (such as the lymph nodes)?

features.label: MUSCULOSKELETAL
features.definition: does the infection affect the muscular system (such as myositis) or the skeletal system (such as osteomyelitis)?

features.label: NEUROLOGICAL
features.definition: does the infection affect the nervous system (such as the brain)?

features.label: REPRODUCTIVE
features.definition: does the infection affect the male or female reproductive system (such as the vagina)?

features.label: RESPIRATORY
features.definition: does the infection affect the respiratory system (such as the lungs)?

features.label: STERILE SITE
features.definition: is the infection site normally sterile (e.g. spinal fluid)?

features.label: SYSTEMIC
features.definition: does the infection affect the entire body, rather than a single organ or body part (for instance blood, e.g. sepsis)?

features.label: URINARY
features.definition: does the infection affect the urinary system (such as the urinary tract)?

features.label: AIR
features.definition: is the pathogen species associated with the air, aerosols, vents, ducts, smoke or dust?

features.label: FRESHWATER
features.definition: is the pathogen species associated with lakes, rivers, streams, reservoirs, water storage units/tanks, waterpipes or other freshwater sources?

features.label: MARINE
features.definition: is the pathogen species associated with coastal environments, the ocean, the sea, the beach or estuaries?

features.label: PLANTS
features.definition: is the pathogen species associated with plants, crops, fruits, seeds, nuts, vegetables or vegetable matter?

features.label: PRECIPITATION
features.definition: is the pathogen associated with rain, aerosols and/or extreme weather events such as flooding, hurricanes or storms?

features.label: SEWAGE
features.definition: is the pathogen associated with sewage, septic tanks, slurry or agricultural run-off?

features.label: SOIL
features.definition: is the pathogen species associated with soils or sediments?

features.label: TEMPERATURE
features.definition: is the pathogen associated with increases in temperature, and/or extreme weather events such as heatwaves or wildfires?

features.label: CATHETER
features.definition: is the infection associated with a urinary cathether?

features.label: INTUBATION
features.definition: is the infection associated with the mouth, teeth, tongue, vocal cords or airway as a result of ventilation?

features.label: OINTMENT
features.definition: is the infection associated with a dressing, salve or oitnment?

features.label: REPLACEMENT
features.definition: is the infection associated with an implant (such as a hip- or heartvalve replacement)?

features.label: NOSOCOMIAL
features.definition: is there evidence that the infection was healthcare associated (e.g. acquired in the hospital)?

features.label: OPERATION
features.definition: is the infection associated with an operation?

features.label: OPPORTUNISTIC
features.definition: is the pathogen referred to as being opportunistic?

features.label: OUTBREAKS
features.definition: are multiple infections reported at the same time as the result of (local) clusters or outbreaks?

features.label: POLYMICROBIAL
features.definition: are multiple pathogens associated with the infection site?

features.label: DYSBIOSIS
features.definition: is the presence of the pathogen associated with an imbalance in bacterial composition, changes in bacterial metabolic activities, or changes in bacterial distribution?

features.label: GEOGRAPHY
features.definition: does the abstract report the city, village, or country where the patient fell ill?

features.label: IMMUNOLOGY
features.definition: is the bacterial species  referred to in the context of the host immune response, virulence factors or molecular interactions?

features.label: MICROBIOME
features.definition: the bacterial species is referred to in studies sequencing the human microbiome, specifically whether its presence or abundance is positively or negatively correlated with other (non-communicable) diseases?

features.label: RECREATION
features.definition: is the infection mentioned in the context of outdoor activities such as swimming or hiking?

features.label: ALCOHOL
features.definition: does the infected patient suffer from alcoholism?

features.label: CYSTIC FIBROSIS
features.definition: does the infected patient suffer from the underlying condition cystic fibrosis?

features.label: DIABETES
features.definition: does the infected patient suffer from the underlying condition diabetes?

features.label: DRUGS
features.definition: is the infected patient an (intravenous) drug user?

features.label: IMMUNOCOMPROMISED
features.definition: is the infected patient immunocompromised or not immunocompetent?

features.label: IMMUNOSUPPRESSED
features.definition: is he epatient immunocompromised, for example as the result of undergoing chemotherapy or radiotherapy?

features.label: PATIENT AGE
features.definition: does the abstract report the infected patient's age or age group (neonate, child, adult, or elderly)?

features.label: PATIENT OCCUPATION
features.definition: does the abstract report the patient's job, role, or occupation?

features.label: SMOKING
features.definition: does the infected patient smoke tobacco?

features.label: EPIDEMIOLOGY
features.definition: the pathogen is discussed in the context of epidemiological surveillance, and strategies and measures aimed at monitoring, preventing, and controlling the spread of infectious diseases (public health interventions)?

features.label: PRIORITY SPECIES
features.definition: is the pathogen species listed as an emerging infectious disease or as a species of high priority to public health?

features.label: VACCINE
features.definition: is the pathogen mentioned in the context of immunization or vaccination?

features.label: AIRBORNE
features.definition: was the infection acquired due to inhalation of cells, aerosols or droplets in the air?

features.label: BITE
features.definition: is the infection associated with an animal bite or wound (such as from a dog, rat or reptile)?

features.label: DIRECT CONTACT
features.definition: can the infection be transmitted via human-to-human contact (touch)?

features.label: FECAL-ORAL
features.definition: was the infection acquired via the faecal-oral route (i.e. unsanitary conditions)?

features.label: FOMITE
features.definition: was the infecion acquired via physical contact with an inanimate object?

features.label: FOODBORNE
features.definition: was the infection acquired through the ingestion of food or drink?

features.label: SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED
features.definition: is the infection associated with sexual contact?

features.label: VECTORBORNE
features.definition: is the disease transmitted by blood-feeding anthropods such as mosquitoes, ticks or fleas?

features.label: VERTICAL
features.definition: can the infection be transmitted from mother to child?

features.label: WATERBORNE
features.definition: was the infection acquired through contact with contaminated water?

features.label: WOUND
features.definition: is the infection assciated with a wound resulting from an accident (but not a bite)?

features.label: ZOONOSIS
features.definition: is the disease transmissable from vertebrate animals to humans?
